title: Corepresenting Hom bijections from compatible cokernel presentations
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor, and let $d:P_2\to P_1$ and $q:P_1\to B$ be morphisms in $\mathcal B$ with $q$ a cokernel of $d$. For $i=1,2$, let $L_i\in\mathcal A$ and let $\theta_{i,X}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(L_i,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(P_i,R(X))$ be bijections natural in $X$, so $\theta_{i,X'}(u\circ a)=R(u)\circ\theta_{i,X}(a)$ for $u:X\to X'$. Assume $\theta_{i,X}(0)=0$. Let $D:L_2\to L_1$ satisfy $\theta_{2,X}(a\circ D)=\theta_{1,X}(a)\circ d$ for every $X$ and $a:L_1\to X$. For any cokernel $c:L_1\to C$ of $D$, there is a unique family of bijections $\psi_X:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(C,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(B,R(X))$ characterized by $\psi_X(v)\circ q=\theta_{1,X}(v\circ c)$. Its inverse sends $b:B\to R(X)$ to the unique $v:C\to X$ satisfying $v\circ c=\theta_{1,X}^{-1}(b\circ q)$. These bijections are natural in $X$: for every $u:X\to X'$ and $v:C\to X$, one has $\psi_{X'}(u\circ v)=R(u)\circ\psi_X(v)$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof: last paragraph, the displayed Hom identifications, with their naturality and the inverse factorization made explicit.

proof.text: Fix $X$. In an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], a cokernel is the coequalizer of its arrow and the parallel zero arrow. Thus the colimit definition [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], applied to this finite parallel-pair diagram, says that maps killing the arrow factor uniquely through its cokernel. For $v:C\to X$, put $a=v\circ c$. Since $c\circ D=0$, compatibility and zero preservation give $\theta_{1,X}(a)\circ d=\theta_{2,X}(a\circ D)=\theta_{2,X}(0)=0$. The cokernel property of $q$ therefore gives a unique $b:B\to R(X)$ with $b\circ q=\theta_{1,X}(v\circ c)$; define $\psi_X(v)=b$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, final paragraph: the three displayed Hom identifications.

proof.text: Conversely, for $b:B\to R(X)$ put $a=\theta_{1,X}^{-1}(b\circ q)$. Then $\theta_{2,X}(a\circ D)=\theta_{1,X}(a)\circ d=b\circ q\circ d=0=\theta_{2,X}(0)$. Injectivity of $\theta_{2,X}$ gives $a\circ D=0$. The unique-factorization clause of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for the cokernel $c$ supplies a unique $v:C\to X$ with $v\circ c=a$. This defines the asserted inverse candidate $\chi_X(b)$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, final paragraph: the three displayed Hom identifications.

proof.text: For $v:C\to X$, the defining equations give $\chi_X(\psi_X(v))\circ c=\theta_{1,X}^{-1}(\psi_X(v)\circ q)=v\circ c$, so uniqueness of factorization through $c$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\chi_X(\psi_X(v))=v$. For $b:B\to R(X)$, they give $\psi_X(\chi_X(b))\circ q=\theta_{1,X}(\chi_X(b)\circ c)=b\circ q$, so the same uniqueness for $q$ gives $\psi_X(\chi_X(b))=b$. Thus $\psi_X$ is a bijection with exactly the inverse stated.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, final paragraph: the three displayed Hom identifications.

proof.text: For $u:X\to X'$ and $v:C\to X$, naturality of the supplied $\theta_1$ gives $\psi_{X'}(u\circ v)\circ q=\theta_{1,X'}(u\circ v\circ c)=R(u)\circ\theta_{1,X}(v\circ c)=(R(u)\circ\psi_X(v))\circ q$. Unique factorization through $q$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] proves naturality. Any other family satisfying the required characterization has, for each $X,v$, the same composite with $q$, hence the same value by this uniqueness. This proves uniqueness of the entire family.
